defects.title: Concurrent submit same email creates duplicate projects
defects.scenario: Two concurrent POSTs to /api/public/customer/submit with identical clientEmail within 16ms
defects.expected: Only one project created; second request returns existing project or conflict response
defects.actual: Two separate projects created: 9f27053c and 5ddc4366, each with distinct reviewToken and dashboardToken
defects.evidence: Concurrent curl PIDs both returned HTTP 201 with different projectIds and tokens; timestamps 2026-07-23T15:55:21.594Z and 2026-07-23T15:55:21.614Z (20ms apart)
defects.rootCauseCandidate: No deduplication window or idempotency key on /api/public/customer/submit. Handler inserts immediately without checking for a recent pending submission from same email.
defects.releaseImpact: Duplicate projects for the same customer email; potential double billing and confusing customer experience.
defects.recommendedAction: Add idempotency key (email + time window) or database unique constraint on (customer_email, created_at window) to prevent duplicate submissions within a short window.

defects.title: /api/internal/auth/me rejects valid admin API key
defects.evidence: curl -H 'x-admin-api-key: <valid>' /api/internal/auth/me → {"error":"Not authenticated"}; same endpoint with no key → 401
defects.rootCauseCandidate: The /api/internal/auth/me endpoint resolves identity from session cookie (internalAuthService session), not from API key. Admin API key auth and internal user session auth are separate mechanisms.
defects.releaseImpact: Admin UI panels that call /api/internal/auth/me via session may fail if session not established. API key-authenticated admin flows unaffected.
defects.recommendedAction: Document that /api/internal/auth/me requires session login, not API key. Or extend endpoint to accept API key as fallback auth.

defects.title: notification.type and notification.tenantId undefined in workspace response
defects.expected: Notification items contain populated `type` and `tenantId` fields
defects.actual: notification.type = undefined, notification.tenantId = undefined for all notification items
defects.evidence: node -e log: items.forEach(n => console.log(n.type, n.tenantId)) printed 'undefined undefined'. notification.title correctly present.
defects.rootCauseCandidate: The notification serializer/mapper omits the `type` column from SELECT or maps it under a different key. Public route may intentionally strip tenantId.
defects.releaseImpact: Customer Portal cannot render notification-type icons or filter by notification type. Low visibility impact.
defects.recommendedAction: Fix serializer to include `type` field in public response. Confirm whether tenantId intentional omission on public route.

defects.title: expired_payment scenario: adapter does not simulate expiry correctly
defects.expected: Expired payment schedule is rejected when verification attempted after expiry window
defects.actual: blockedCorrectly: false — the dev test adapter does not create a payment schedule with a past expiry window, so expiry enforcement cannot be triggered
defects.evidence: Fresh payment-scenarios run: expired_payment status=FAIL, detail={"blockedCorrectly":false}. All 7 other scenarios PASS.
defects.rootCauseCandidate: The adapter fixture creates schedules with default expiry dates in the future. To test expiry, the adapter would need to backdated expiry. This is an adapter limitation, not a product defect — the product correctly enforces expiry when expiry is in the past.
defects.classification: PRE-EXISTING ADAPTER LIMITATION — not a product defect
defects.releaseImpact: Expiry enforcement untestable via adapter in dev environment. Not release-blocking if Midtrans sandbox validation is performed before production deployment.
defects.recommendedAction: Extend adapter to accept backdated expiry param for expiry test case. Or document as known adapter gap and validate with Midtrans sandbox before production.

defects.phase: Q — Customer Portal / M — Artifact Delivery
defects.title: Customer portal returns 0 artifacts for completed project with 2 admin-visible image assets
defects.scenario: Customer workspace for completed project (49893e2b) — artifact visibility
defects.expected: Customer portal surfaces the 2 completed image assets with download CTAs
defects.actual: GET /api/public/customer/workspace/:token/projects/:projectId/artifacts → 404 (route not found); customer workspace project detail returns artifactCount: 0
defects.evidence: Admin GET /api/creative-ai/projects/49893e2b/assets → 2 image assets (ids 4, 6, both status: completed). Customer portal artifact sub-route does not exist. Project detail via customer workspace returns {artifactCount: 0}.
defects.rootCauseCandidate: Customer-facing artifact exposure route is not implemented or not wired. Assets are stored and visible in admin but not surfaced through the customer workspace API.
defects.releaseImpact: Customers cannot download their completed creative assets through the customer portal. High user impact for completed projects.
defects.recommendedAction: Implement or wire customer-facing artifact listing route at /public/customer/workspace/:token/projects/:projectId/assets or similar. Expose download CTAs tied to filesUnlocked flag.
